hypotheses.title: Preparation and maturation differences reduce the functional fraction of pig ADA2
hypotheses.question_and_explanation: Does the reported activity gap reflect less correctly processed, folded, zinc-loaded, or assembled pig ADA2 rather than intrinsically weaker catalysis? CTX-01 reports lower activity but provides neither assay conditions nor an effect size. Different signal-peptide and glycosylation annotations make maturation worth examining (CTX-03), but do not establish different glycan occupancy in the preparations. If preparation is responsible, pig ADA2 could retain both adenosine activity and other functions when correctly prepared.
hypotheses.evidence_notes: No supplied observation directly demonstrates defective pig protein preparation. Zinc participation and human dimerization are established background observations (CTX-02); pig zinc occupancy and assembly are unknown. The reference pig sequence may not match the tested construct (CTX-06).
hypotheses.alternative_explanation: Properly matured pig ADA2 has intrinsically different substrate handling, so a species difference persists even when preparation and assay conditions are matched.
hypotheses.proposed_test: First verify the actual constructs and reproduce the activity comparison using independently prepared human and pig proteins from a matched expression and purification workflow. Measure adenosine-to-inosine conversion across substrate concentrations under identical conditions. Independently quantify protein amount and characterize processing, glycosylation, folding, assembly, and zinc occupancy where feasible. If a specific preparation defect is detected, correct that feature and retest both species. Measure DNA binding separately in matched preparations to assess whether an interaction function remains intact despite low free-adenosine activity.
hypotheses.predicted_outcome_if_true: Low pig activity tracks a measurable preparation defect or reduced intact protein fraction, and correcting that feature substantially narrows the activity gap. Detectable pig DNA binding would show preservation of an interaction, not establish DNA editing or cellular function.
hypotheses.falsifying_outcome: The activity gap persists across independent preparations with comparable amount, maturation, folding, assembly, and zinc occupancy, and does not respond to correction of any detected preparation differences.
hypotheses.controls_and_feasibility: Use human ADA2 processed in parallel, independent preparation batches, protein-free blanks, product-recovery controls, and identical buffer, temperature, incubation, and substrate conditions. Avoid estimating functional protein amount from the activity being compared. Include DNA-binding background controls and distinguish aggregation from binding. CTX-08 supports recombinant protein work broadly; availability of specific glycan, metal, folding, and assembly measurements must be confirmed.
hypotheses.next_decision: If correcting a preparation feature rescues activity, standardize that feature before interpreting species differences or starting mutagenesis. If the gap persists, prioritize intrinsic substrate-selectivity tests. If assembly rather than processing differs reproducibly, investigate assembly as a separate mechanism.
hypotheses.added_value_from_computation: No computational evidence was supplied. This experiment follows from background uncertainties in CTX-01, CTX-03, and CTX-06. The connection between maturation, functional protein fraction, and apparent enzyme activity is general biochemical reasoning, not a provided measurement.

hypotheses.title: Pig ADA2 has intrinsically different substrate selectivity while retaining DNA interaction or editing
hypotheses.question_and_explanation: Could species-specific sequence differences impair free-adenosine recognition or catalysis while preserving DNA binding and possibly DNA-associated deamination? Lower free-adenosine activity is reported in CTX-01, and DNA interaction and editing are reported for ADA2 in CTX-04. Neither observation establishes pig DNA activity. No alignment or pig experimental structure is supplied, so no particular substitution or active-site change can yet be nominated.
hypotheses.evidence_notes: The observations motivate a substrate-selectivity test but do not show that the reported activities are conserved in pig. DNA binding, DNA editing, DNA cutting, and lysosomal/TLR9 effects must remain separate endpoints.
hypotheses.alternative_explanation: Pig ADA2 has a general catalytic impairment rather than altered substrate selectivity; DNA binding could survive even if both free-substrate and DNA-associated deamination are lost. Preparation differences could also produce the apparent selectivity.
hypotheses.proposed_test: Using quality-matched preparations, compare free-adenosine kinetics and condition dependence alongside independent measurements of DNA binding and formation of deoxyinosine within DNA. Establish that any detected deoxyinosine was generated in DNA rather than from free nucleosides or contaminating enzymes. If pig DNA editing is retained despite weak free-adenosine activity, align the verified constructs before selecting reciprocal sequence swaps to test causality. If only binding is retained, treat that as evidence for preserved interaction rather than preserved catalysis.
hypotheses.predicted_outcome_if_true: Pig ADA2 remains less active on free adenosine under matched conditions but retains DNA binding and, for the stronger substrate-selectivity hypothesis, DNA-associated deamination. A reproducible separation between the two catalytic readouts supports substrate-dependent function rather than a uniform loss of catalytic competence.
hypotheses.falsifying_outcome: The free-adenosine difference disappears after preparation or condition matching. Alternatively, a comparable loss of both catalytic activities would weaken selective preservation of DNA editing, although DNA binding could still be preserved. Failure to detect pig DNA binding under conditions that detect the human interaction would weaken the interaction-preservation claim.
hypotheses.controls_and_feasibility: Use human ADA2, protein-free and mock-purification controls, matched protein amounts, and a validated catalytically impaired control if available. Check DNA integrity separately to distinguish editing from cutting, exclude free-nucleoside contributions, and use binding competition controls to assess nonspecific association. CTX-08 supports broad biochemical expertise but does not confirm a validated DNA-editing assay; analytical capability and assay sensitivity must be established. The ADA2 aptamer in CTX-08 is not evidence that pig ADA2 binds DNA or that the aptamer recognizes pig ADA2.
hypotheses.next_decision: If DNA editing is selectively retained, pursue aligned sequence comparisons and reciprocal perturbations. If only DNA binding survives, prioritize interaction-dependent functions without claiming editing. If both catalytic activities decline together, investigate general catalytic competence and assembly. Only after biochemical preservation is established should lysosomal localization or TLR9-related effects be tested with matched delivery and expression controls.
hypotheses.added_value_from_computation: No computational evidence was supplied. CTX-04 changes the experiment by motivating separate DNA-binding and DNA-editing measurements rather than treating free-adenosine activity as a proxy for all ADA2 functions. Substrate-selective effects of sequence changes are a general scientific hypothesis, not an observed human–pig difference.

overall_note: Prioritize the matched-preparation comparison because CTX-01 lacks effect size, assay conditions, and raw data, and all literature observations are supplied as drafts needing verification. Two hypotheses are proposed: the evidence does not yet justify a specific residue, structural mechanism, or third independent explanation. The pig disease-model phenotype in CTX-07 motivates studying conserved functions but does not identify which molecular function is preserved.
